title: CHAPTER FOURTEEN. On the Lord's Supper: definition
latin: CAPUT DECIMUM QUARTUM, De coena Domini. COENA DOMINI est sacramentum N.T. ab ipso Christo immediate in usum Ecclesiae ad finem usque mundi institutum, in quo legitima panis & vini externa administratione, sumptione, manducatione & haustione mors Domini annunciatur, interne corporis & sanguinis Christi sumptio & fruitio exhibetur, & arctissima illa unio sive koinonia qua sumus cum Christo capite nostro coniuncti obsignatur & confirmatur; fideles vero suam erga Deum gratitudinem & obligationem, communionem inter ipsos & ab aliis separationem profitentur.
english: CHAPTER FOURTEEN. On the Lord's Supper.

The LORD'S SUPPER is a New Testament sacrament instituted by Christ Himself immediately for the Church's use until the world's end, in which by lawful external administration, taking, eating, and drinking of bread and wine the Lord's death is announced; inwardly the taking and fruition of Christ's body and blood are exhibited; and that closest union or koinonia by which we are joined to Christ our Head is sealed and confirmed; while the faithful profess their gratitude and obligation toward God, communion among themselves, and separation from others.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye LORD'S SUPPER stands as a New Testament sacrament instituted by Christ Himself immediately for ye Church's use until ye world's end, in which by lawful external administration, taking, eating, and drinking belonging toward bread and wine ye Lord's death stands as announced; inwardly ye taking and fruition belonging toward Christ's body and blood stand as exhibited; and that closest union or koinonia by which we stand as joined toward Christ our Head stands as sealed and confirmed; while ye faithful profess their gratitude and obligation toward God, communion among themselves, and separation from others. — CHAPTER FOURTEEN. On ye Lord's Supper.

title: True exhibition of body and blood; against mere-bread charge
latin: Iniurii igitur sunt in ecclesiarum nostrarum doctrinam qui criminantur nos merum panem & vinum mere coelesti in coena statuere. Nam Joh. Calvin. Inst. 4.17: Dicimus Christum tam externo symbolo quam spiritu suo ad nos descendere, ut vere substantia carnis suae & sanguinis sui animas nostras vivificet. Exclusa igitur transsubstantiatione & consubstantiatione sive impanatione, particulas illas cum, sua, cum antiquis sano sensu facile admittimus, ad declarandam veram quidem sed mysticam rerum signatarum praesentiam & in legitimo sacramenti usu exhibitionem.
english: Those who charge our churches' doctrine with setting mere bread and wine as merely heavenly in the Supper do us injury. For Calvin (Inst. 4.17) says we affirm that Christ descends to us by the external symbol as well as by His Spirit, so that He truly vivifies our souls by the substance of His flesh and blood.

Transubstantiation and consubstantiation or impanation excluded, we readily admit with the ancients in a sound sense those particles with / under / in, to declare a presence of the things signified that is true yet mystical, and their exhibition in lawful use of the sacrament.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Transubstantiation and consubstantiation or impanation excluded, we readily admit with ye ancients in a sound sense those particles with / under / in, toward declare a presence belonging toward ye things signified that stands as true yet mystical, and their exhibition in lawful use belonging toward ye sacrament. — Those who charge our churches' doctrine with setting mere bread and wine as merely heavenly in ye Supper do us injury. For Calvin (Inst. 4.17) says we affirm that Christ descends toward us by ye external symbol as well as by His Spirit, so that He truly vivifies our souls by ye substance belonging toward His flesh and blood.

title: Sacramental presence not local or physical; no conversion of elements
latin: 4. Corpus & sanguis Christi neque localiter neque ullo modo physico, sed vere ac realiter, sine fictione ulla in coena praesentia sunt, unita cum pane & vino unione sacramentali per analogiam & relationem mysticam. Non est hic ulla enousia inexistentiae vel synousia coexistentiae per indistinquam localem. 5. Panis benedictus non convertitur aut transmutatur in corpus Christi, nec vinum in sanguinem, sed sicuti ante, ita etiam in unione sacramentali essentia utrobique distincta manent—quia Scriptura nominat panem post consecrationem (Matth. 26:26; 1 Cor. 11:26-28); quia panis est koinonia corporis Christi; quia Christus non dixit hoc fiat sed hoc est corpus meum.
english: 4. Christ's body and blood are present in the Supper neither locally nor in any physical mode, but truly and really without any fiction, united with bread and wine by sacramental union through analogy and mystical relation—not by local inexistence or coexistence.

5. Blessed bread is not converted or transmuted into Christ's body, nor wine into blood; essences remain distinct on both sides even in sacramental union—because Scripture still names bread after consecration (Matt. 26:26; 1 Cor. 11:26-28); because bread is the communion of Christ's body; because Christ said not let this become but this is my body.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): 5. Blessed bread stands as not converted or transmuted into Christ's body, nor wine into blood; essences remain distinct on both sides even in sacramental union—because Scripture still names bread after consecration (Matt. 26:26; 1 Cor. 11:26-28); because bread stands as ye communion belonging toward Christ's body; because Christ said not let this become but this stands as my body. — 4. Christ's body and blood stand as present in ye Supper neither locally nor in any physical mode, but truly and really without any fiction, united with bread and wine by sacramental union through analogy and mystical relation—not by local inexistence or coexistence.

title: Worthy and unworthy eating; pastoral severity (Chrysostom)
latin: Manducatio sacramentalis secundum obiecta distinguenda est. Indigni accedentes iudicium sibi manducant & bibunt (1 Cor. 11:27-29). Chrysostomus horribiliter monet ministros ne Dominum irritent corpus non purgando: Animum prius tradam meam, quam dominicum alicui corpus indigne; sanguinemque meum effundi potius patiar, quam sacratissimum illum sanguinem praeter quam digno concedam. Multo daemoniaco peior est qui peccati sibi conscius accedit.
english: Sacramental eating is to be distinguished according to its objects. Those who approach unworthily eat and drink judgment to themselves (1 Cor. 11:27-29).

Chrysostom terribly warns ministers not to provoke the Lord by failing to purge the body: I would sooner give up my life than give the Lord's body to anyone unworthily; I would rather have my blood poured out than grant that most sacred blood except to one who is worthy. Far worse than a demoniac is the one who approaches conscious of sin.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Chrysostom terribly warns ministers not toward provoke ye Lord by failing toward purge ye body: I would sooner give up my life than give ye Lord's body toward anyone unworthily; I would rather have my blood poured out than grant that most sacred blood except toward one who stands as worthy. Far worse than a demoniac stands as ye one who approaches conscious belonging toward sin. — Sacramental eating stands as toward be distinguished according toward its objects. Those who approach unworthily eat and drink judgment toward themselves (1 Cor. 11:27-29).

title: Frequency; infants; Cap.15 next on the ministry of the word
latin: 13. Veri Christiani non pro more & propter consuetudinem usurpant sacram coenam, sed ex ardenti Christi desiderio alacriter ac religiose, ut praecepto ipsius satisfaciant, dilectione & thesauro fruantur, tum ob suam etiam necessitatem frequenter, ut infirmam fidem roborent. In primitiva ecclesia fideles quotidie communicabant (Acts; Cyprian; Augustine); postmodum deminuto fidei ardore mos ille obsolvit. De parvulis: cum ad hoc mysterium requiratur sui probatio & mortis Domini annunciatio (1 Cor. 11), institutio huius sacramenti non per se pertinet ad parvulos qui haec praestare nequeunt. CAPUT DECIMUM QUINTUM sequitur, De ministerio verbi.
english: 13. True Christians do not use the sacred Supper by custom alone, but eagerly and religiously from ardent desire for Christ, that they may satisfy His precept, enjoy His love and treasure, and frequently also for their own need, to strengthen weak faith. In the primitive church the faithful communicated daily; later, as faith's ardor cooled, that custom faded.
As for little ones: since this mystery requires self-examination and announcing the Lord's death (1 Cor. 11), the institution does not of itself pertain to infants who cannot perform these.
CHAPTER FIFTEEN follows, On the ministry of the word.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER FIFTEEN follows, On ye ministry belonging toward ye word. — As for little ones: since this mystery requires self-examination and announcing ye Lord's death (1 Cor. 11), ye institution does not belonging toward itself pertain toward infants who cannot perform these. — 13. True Christians do not use ye sacred Supper by custom alone, but eagerly and religiously from ardent desire for Christ, that they may satisfy His precept, enjoy His love and treasure, and frequently also for their own need, toward strengthen weak faith. In ye primitive church ye faithful communicated daily; later, as faith's ardor cooled, that custom faded.
